subject: Service guarantee exclusions — moderation/tool-calling/structured-output
messages:
From: Jennifer Su <jennifer.su@acme-fin.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Financial Procurement <contracts@acme-fin.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: Clarify SLA carve-outs for moderation/tool failures

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending the main SLA earlier. Our legal team flagged a couple of edge cases we need explicit language for before we can sign — specifically around availability/uptime measurements when calls to customer-provided tools fail, and when Redwood’s content moderation filters block or truncate outputs (which can cause structured output parsers to error).

Two quick questions: 1) Will Redwood exclude downtime/latency impacts caused by third-party tool integrations (e.g., webhook timeouts, external vector DBs) from the uptime calculation? 2) How do you treat incidents where the model returns data but the response is altered or blocked by content filtering or structured-output schema enforcement — do those count as an SLA failure?

We’d like proposed contract wording we can circulate internally. Happy to jump on a quick call if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Jennifer Su
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Financial

---
Attachments: none
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Su <jennifer.su@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify SLA carve-outs for moderation/tool failures

Hi Jennifer — thanks for the clear questions. Below is proposed language we use for customers with similar compliance needs. I’m copying Marissa (AM), Evelyn (CS) and Vivek (Legal) so we can align quickly.

Proposed SLA exclusion language (draft):
- Exclusions: Availability and latency calculations for Redwood’s Service do not apply to periods where unavailability or degraded performance is caused by (a) third-party integrations and downstream services beyond Redwood’s control (including customer-managed tool endpoints, external vector stores, webhook targets, or partner APIs); (b) automated content moderation or policy enforcement that blocks, redacts, or truncates model-generated content; or (c) client-side or customer-provided parsing and structured-output validation failures that occur after Redwood has returned a response in accordance with the requested model and configuration.

- Operational notes: Redwood will surface detected moderation events and tool-call failures in the Console and in Trace logs. For incidents where moderation or tool failures materially affect output quality, Redwood will classify the event as an operational incident (for visibility and remediation) but will not count those periods toward SLA uptime credits unless Redwood’s runtime, networking, or hosting layers are confirmed to be the proximate cause.

We can provide a short addendum to the master services agreement with the above wording. I’ll attach an editable addendum and a sample DocuSign route if that helps accelerate review.

Would you like us to: (A) send the addendum for your redline, or (B) propose slightly softer wording that still preserves availability protections for your end-users?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify SLA carve-outs for moderation/tool failures

Looping in a quick note from Sales & CS perspective. Karthik — proposed language is concise and aligned with our policy. Two small tweaks I’d suggest before we send to Acme for redline:

1) Add a sentence ensuring Redwood will provide a post-incident analysis and remediation timeline for moderation/tool events that have operational impact (we want to preserve our obligation to investigate).
2) Clarify that structured-output validation failures will be excluded only when the schema enforcement occurs downstream of Redwood’s canonical response (i.e., exclusions do not apply when Redwood’s model invocation or runtime truncation is the proximate cause).

Suggested inline addition: "Redwood will investigate reported incidents involving moderation or tool-call failures and provide a remediation plan within a commercially reasonable timeframe (typically 3 business days for initial triage). An exclusion to SLA credit will only apply where evidence shows the proximate cause is outside Redwood's runtime, hosting, or networking infrastructure."

Vivek: PTAL for legal language. Evelyn: want you to confirm the Console traces we surface will be sufficient for ACME's procurement/legal team to validate root cause.

-Marissa

marissa@redwood.com

We circulated internally and attached a redline with two asks: (1) add a requirement that Redwood provide exportable incident logs for moderation/tool events tied to the affected customer requests, and (2) limit the exclusion for structured-output validation failures to cases where a customer-provided schema/validator was explicitly configured and applied.

I attached our redline (ACME_redline_SLA_Addendum.docx) with inline comments. If you can accept those two changes we can route for signature. Also prefer DocuSign route for the addendum.

Jennifer — appreciate the quick turnaround and the redlines. We reviewed internally with Legal and CS; we can accept both asks with minor wording to keep operational clarity. I’ve attached the signed addendum (PDF stub) and opened a DocuSign envelope for your execution. Link below.

Accepted/final items in the addendum:
- Exportable incident logs: Redwood will provide, upon request, exportable logs that include request id, timestamp, model variant, moderation flags applied (if any), and tool-call error codes for incidents tied to the affected customer requests. Redwood will redact any content that is subject to regulatory or privacy restrictions prior to export in accordance with the MSA.
- Structured-output exclusion scoping: The exclusion for structured-output validation failures applies only when a customer-specified schema or external validator is applied downstream of Redwood's canonical response. If evidence shows Redwood's runtime truncated or altered the canonical response such that validation would have otherwise succeeded, the exclusion will not apply.
